problem: Zero-shot ObjectNav methods treat semantic cues (priors, detections, contextual relations) as reliably positive evidence with no way to assess or revise their influence, so false detections, category confusion and failed visits keep biasing frontier selection toward unproductive regions.
motivation: Open-vocabulary perception is noisy in indoor scenes (small, occluded or look-alike objects), and static priors or accumulated map evidence are hard to revise once they influence decisions. Semantic cues are relational and carry both supportive evidence (co-occurring objects) and contradictory evidence (look-alike distractors, failed access), so guidance should be strengthened or weakened online.
key_idea: Factorize target-centric semantic relations into activation and inhibition roles and propagate them over a local graph to reshape frontier scores, with a reliability-aware gate deciding when to commit to a target.
insight: Both signs of evidence matter, and role assignment must be robust to noisy labels. On HM3Dv2, removing activation bias drops SR from 74.5 to 65.4, and removing multi-label competition drops it to 66.7; removing similar-object inhibition or failed access costs 4.7 and 3.2 SR. SER-Nav also gains more than the baselines from the same detectors (57.3 SR with G-DINO alone vs VLFM 45.6, ApexNav 43.7), and random relations drop SR to 61.2, so the gains come from meaningful relations rather than stronger perception. An LLM is used only offline to generate the relation set.
method: Target-centric category-role vector: each category gets a binary vector [commit, activate, inhibit]; target/synonyms are [1,1,0], contextual co-occurring objects [0,1,0], visually similar distractors [0,0,1]. The relation set is generated offline by DeepSeek.

Multi-label object-role competition: each object cluster keeps several label hypotheses scored by multi-view support times confidence reliability; the argmax label is chosen and its strength sigma(rho) scales the role vector into object-level evidence h_o.

Relational activation–inhibition propagation: a local graph of object, contextual hypothesis, negative-evidence and frontier nodes, with a distance-decayed kernel exp(-d/R) within radius R. Activation A(f) sums commitment evidence and hypothesis nodes; inhibition I(f) sums distractor evidence and negative-evidence nodes.
Failed-access memory: a frontier visited without a reliable target candidate creates or strengthens a negative-evidence node that decays over time and can be overridden by new consistent evidence.
Bias-conditioned frontier scoring: S~(f) = (S0(f) + A(f)) / (1 + I(f) + normalized path cost), where S0 is the BLIP-2 semantic value; the argmax frontier is chosen.

Reliability-aware commitment gate: commit to the object with the highest commitment evidence when it is at least theta (0.45), then approach it with an A* local planner; otherwise keep exploring. R=2.3 is the default radius.

setting.backbone: YOLO + GroundingDINO + MobileSAM + BLIP-2 (frozen perception stack, following ApexNav); no online LLM; DeepSeek generates the relation set offline
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D with pose, perception range 0-5 m
setting.action_space: discrete low-level: MoveForward 0.25 m, TurnLeft/Right 30°, Stop; 500-step budget; A* local planner
setting.simulator: Habitat (HM3Dv1, HM3Dv2, MP3D); real-world Wheeltec R550 robot

numbers.extra: HM3Dv2 version; no online LLM; relation set from DeepSeek offline

numbers_note: The paper does not name splits explicitly; HM3Dv1 and the ablations are labelled 'val', and 'val' is assumed for the main table. A separate efficiency table reports HM3D SR 60.5, 0.0 LLM calls, 144.0 steps and 101.8 s per episode. Hyperparameter sensitivity is given only in a figure.
results: SER-Nav reaches 74.5 SR / 36.8 SPL on HM3Dv2 (VLFM: 63.6 / 32.5), 60.5 / 32.1 on HM3Dv1 (best baseline MFNP: 58.3 / 26.7), and 42.1 / 19.2 on MP3D (best baseline UniGoal: 41.0 SR, CoS: 17.6 SPL). It uses no online LLM calls and 101.8 s per episode, versus 190.3 s for ASCENT.
limitations: Relation sets (context and distractors) come from an offline LLM prompt and are per-category; random relations drop SR to 61.2, so quality matters.
The perception stack (YOLO, GroundingDINO, MobileSAM, BLIP-2) is heavy and needs a remote GPU for the real robot; the real-world evaluation is only qualitative (two tasks).
Gains on MP3D are small, and the hyperparameters R and theta were tuned on HM3Dv2 val.
